source_checkout.note: repo/ at head; base is an ancestor. No node_modules installed, so dependency contents (protect-ffi 0.24.0, auth 0.38.0) could not be inspected.

pr_description.note: Only the title is given in CASE.md.

summary: Adds a new ESM-only `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` subpath (minimal encrypt/decrypt client over protect-ffi's WASM build) plus a Deno CI smoke test and a Supabase example. The release risk is mostly not in the new subpath but in what moves with it for every existing consumer: protect-ffi is bumped 0.23.0 -> 0.24.0 under the main Node entry (with a new node/default conditional-exports split, per the author's tsconfig comment), the main build now bundles zod and @byteslice/result, @cipherstash/auth moves 0.36 -> 0.38 for the shipped CLI and wizard, and the stack version is bumped by hand to 0.18.0 even though the repo releases via changesets and a pending minor changeset exists, with no changeset for this change. The WASM client also drops the Node entry's null short-circuit, so a null plaintext is encrypted rather than passed through. No CI results were available and protect-ffi/auth changelogs could not be read, so compatibility of 0.24 payloads with the EQL 2.3.1 bundle is unknown.

behaviour_changes.description: New published subpath `./wasm-inline` (import condition only, no require) exporting Encryption, WasmEncryptionClient, schema builders and isEncrypted. The client exposes only encrypt/decrypt that return raw values and throw on error, unlike the Node entry's Result objects; it has no lock context, bulk or query operations.

@cipherstash/protect-ffi bumped 0.23.0 -> 0.24.0 for the main Node entry used by all stack consumers. Per the author's tsconfig comment, 0.24 uses conditional exports where `node` selects NAPI and `default` selects the WASM bundle with a different newClient signature.

tsup main config switches clean:true -> clean:false (dist cleared by a new prebuild script) and adds zod and @byteslice/result to noExternal, so these are bundled into every main-entry ESM/CJS output, not only wasm-inline.
packages/stack version set manually 0.17.0 -> 0.18.0 with no changeset added; the repo releases via changesets and an unreleased minor changeset for stack is already pending.

@cipherstash/auth catalog bumped 0.36.0 -> 0.38.0 (used at runtime by the shipped CLI login/init and wizard prerequisites); cli and wizard now declare six per-platform auth binaries as optionalDependencies because auth 0.38 makes them optional peers. stack gains @cipherstash/auth as a runtime dependency.
WASM client encrypt passes plaintext straight to protect-ffi, and WasmPlaintext explicitly admits null; the Node entry short-circuits null to null.

New CI job wasm-e2e-tests builds stack and runs a Deno round-trip without FFI permission; it fails if the CS_* secrets are absent (e.g. fork PRs). The integration-test Postgres image stays on EQL 2.3.1, which the workflow comment says is tied to protect-ffi 0.23.x.

pnpm-lock.yaml regenerated; besides the auth/protect-ffi updates it drops `libc:` constraints from many platform packages, suggesting a different pnpm version produced it. Affects repo installs only, not published packages.

failure_scenarios.title: protect-ffi 0.24 changes main-entry behaviour or payloads without the EQL/CLI lockstep bump
failure_scenarios.trigger: A stack consumer upgrades to the release carrying this change, or bundles the main entry with a bundler whose conditions omit `node`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/stack/package.json:217 moves protect-ffi to 0.24.0. The workflow comment (tests.yml:21-25) says the EQL image is pinned to match the payload format of protect-ffi 0.23.x and must be bumped in lockstep; it is not, and the CLI still installs eql-2.3.1. The author's tsconfig comment says 0.24 resolves `default` to the WASM bundle with a different newClient signature, so a consumer bundle resolving without the `node` condition would call the NAPI-style newClient({...}) (encryption/index.ts:81) against the WASM API. The dependency's own changelog was not available.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If 0.24 changed payload or search-term shape, newly written ciphertexts or query terms may not match what EQL 2.3.1 in customer databases or older clients expect (wrong query results). With a non-node bundle, client initialisation fails for that deployment.

failure_scenarios.title: Manual 0.18.0 bump collides with changesets; example's ^0.18.0 never resolves

failure_scenarios.mechanism: package.json:3 is set to 0.18.0 by hand while CHANGELOG still tops out at 0.17.0 and .changeset/restore-null-guards-in-encryption-ops.md requests a stack minor bump. changeset version bumps from the current 0.18.0 to 0.19.0, so 0.18.0 is never published, and for a 0.x range `^0.18.0` excludes 0.19.0. No changeset describes the new subpath or the protect-ffi/auth bumps.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Published version skips 0.18.0; the Supabase example import `npm:@cipherstash/stack@^0.18.0/wasm-inline` fails to resolve; the release notes omit a dependency bump that affects every consumer.

failure_scenarios.title: WASM client encrypts null instead of passing it through
failure_scenarios.trigger: An edge/Deno caller encrypts a nullable column value that is null.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: WasmPlaintext includes null (wasm-inline.ts:108-114) and encrypt (wasm-inline.ts:205-218) forwards it to protect-ffi unguarded, whereas the Node EncryptOperation returns null (encrypt.ts:63). The pending changeset states protect-ffi turns null into a real SteVec ciphertext.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A null value is stored as a non-NULL ciphertext; IS NULL queries and code expecting null diverge between data written by edge and Node clients.

missing_verification: Test of encrypt(null)/decrypt(null) on the WASM entry matching Node entry semantics.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add the same null short-circuit to WasmEncryptionClient.encrypt/decrypt, or remove null from WasmPlaintext.

failure_scenarios.title: auth 0.38 bump breaks CLI login or wizard credential detection
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer runs `stash auth login`/init or the wizard on a release built with auth 0.38.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The CLI destructures beginDeviceCodeFlow/bindClientDevice from the auth default export (login.ts:1-4) and the wizard calls AutoStrategy.detect(); auth moves two minor versions and changes how native bindings are packaged (optional peers, compensated by new optionalDependencies). Wizard unit tests mock @cipherstash/auth, so API or binding-load changes are not exercised there. History shows the branch first kept cli/wizard on 0.36.0 and later reversed that.
failure_scenarios.consequence: CLI authentication or wizard prerequisites fail on some or all platforms; loud but customer-facing.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Review auth 0.37/0.38 changelog; pack and install the CLI tarball on macOS/Linux/Windows before release.
